title: Indians Travelling to UAE Advised to Take Medical Insurance With Repatriation Cover
excerpt: India's missions in Abu Dhabi and Dubai issued the advisory after receiving several cases of travellers facing huge hospital bills they could not pay. Cover should be bought before travel, include cashless treatment, and cover medical repatriation to India.
body:
• India's Embassy in Abu Dhabi and Consulate General in Dubai have advised all Indians travelling to the UAE for visit or tourism to take adequate medical insurance before starting their journey.
  • The policy should cover cashless facilities and the cost of medical repatriation to India in the event of an unforeseen medical emergency.
  • The missions said they have received several instances of Indian nationals facing huge medical bills "beyond the capacity of the patient or their family members to bear," with inadequate insurance cover.
  • Action step: buy cover before you board, not on arrival — and if you live in the UAE on an employment visa or as a dependent, verify your existing insurance covers all medical expenses in the UAE plus repatriation to India.

Indian missions in the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday advised Indian nationals travelling to the Gulf nation to take adequate medical insurance, including cover for medical repatriation to India, citing several instances of people facing huge hospital bills that they or their families could not afford, according to IANS.

What the Advisory Says

"All Indian nationals who are travelling to UAE for visit or tourism purposes are hereby advised to take adequate and appropriate medical insurance, prior to commencement of their journey, which also covers cashless facilities including the cost of medical repatriation to India in the event of unforeseen medical emergency."

— Embassy of India, Abu Dhabi and Consulate General of India, Dubai

The advisory, issued by the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi and the Consulate General of India in Dubai and the Northern Emirates, states that the missions "have been receiving several instances of Indian nationals meeting with unforeseen illnesses or medical emergencies resulting in huge medical bills beyond the capacity of the patient or their family members to bear and having inadequate insurance cover." The PTI report carried the same advisory.

Residents Are Covered by the Advice Too

The missions also addressed Indians already living in the country: "Indians residing in UAE on employment visa or as dependents are advised to verify that their medical insurance is adequate to cover all medical expenses in UAE and medical repatriation to India." Employer-provided policies vary widely in network and limits, and dependent cover is a common gap.

Why It Matters

Private hospital care in the UAE is expensive, and an emergency admission or air repatriation can run far beyond what most families can pay out of pocket. The advisory follows a pattern the missions have flagged before — travellers arriving on visit visas without insurance, then turning to the consulate when bills mount. In July, India and the UAE reaffirmed their commitment to ensuring the safety, dignity and well-being of their citizens living in each other's countries at the 7th Meeting of the India-UAE Joint Committee on Consular Affairs. For travellers, the practical takeaway is simple: arrange the policy in India before departure, confirm it includes cashless hospitalisation and repatriation, and keep the policy details accessible to family members travelling with you.
